content: JunD is a transcription factor protein encoded by the JUN D gene in humans. This protein is a member of the JUN family and serves as a functional component of the AP-1 transcription factor complex. It has been suggested that JunD plays a protective role in preventing cells from undergoing p53-dependent senescence and apoptosis. The use of alternative translation initiation sites leads to the production of different isoforms of the JunD protein. The dominant negative mutant variant of JunD, referred to as ΔJunD (Delta JunD), acts as a potent antagonist of the ΔFosB transcript and other forms of AP-1-mediated transcriptional activity, including those induced by ΔFosB. Drugs that inhibit ΔFosB activity may hold potential as effective treatments for addiction and addictive disorders. JunD has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins, including ATF3, MEN1, DNA damage-inducible transcript 3, and BRCA1.
